blocks.text: Condo buildings in Fraserview NW
Palace Quay — 69 and 71 Jamieson Court

The building directory records Palace Quay at 71 Jamieson Court as built in 1992 with 220 units, amenities of elevator, exercise centre, in-suite laundry, indoor pool, recreation centre and swirlpool/hot tub, and strata restrictions of "Pets allowed w/rest., rentals allowed w/restrictions" — the rental line is old bylaw text: a long-term rental-restriction bylaw has been unenforceable in BC since November 24, 2022. Other sources conflict on the year and agree on the builder: a furnished-rental directory records Palace Quay as developed by Bosa Development in 1991, an 18-storey condo at 69–71 Jamieson Court with 220 units, and current listings record the year built variously as 1991, 1992 and 1993 at unit level, with concrete construction and freehold strata title, and one listing recording 2 pets OK with no size restrictions.
Queen's Park Place — 55 Blackberry Drive

A current listing names the building Queen's Park Place, records it built in 1994, and describes it as a quiet 55+ building — a 55+ bylaw is the only age-restriction bylaw valid in BC (SPA ss.123.1/123.2); confirm the filed bylaw and its exemptions on the Form B. Unit count, construction and published pet/rental restrictions: UNCONFIRMED from the sources checked.
Fraserview Park — 74 Miner Street

A current listing records the subdivision name Fraserview Park at this address, built 1989, apartment/condo form, with pets recorded as cats OK at unit level, in the Fraserview NW sub-area. Unit count, construction and a published building-level restriction set: UNCONFIRMED.
Victoria Hill — 15 Royal Avenue (also 15 E Royal Avenue)

The building directory records the building named Victoria Hill at 15 Royal Ave as built in 2007, with restrictions of "Pets allowed w/rest., rentals allowed w/restrictions" (rental line void for long-term rentals —) and amenities of exercise centre, guest suite, in-suite laundry, outdoor pool, recreation centre and swirlpool/hot tub. Current listings describe the Victoria Hill community as by Onni, a Georgie Award-winning master-planned development, with concrete construction at this address. A second Royal Avenue address, 11 E Royal Avenue, is filed by a listing source under the subdivision name "The Residences Of Victoria Hill" — whether 11 and 15 Royal Avenue are one strata or two is UNCONFIRMED from the sources checked, and they are documented as one entry here so the complex is not double-counted; one listing at 14 E Royal Avenue records the building name Victoria Hill with a 2005 year built, so the complex's year is flagged as 2005–2007 across sources, with the directory's 2007 used. Unit count: UNCONFIRMED.
The Lookout at Victoria Hill — 22 East Royal Avenue

A developer-era project profile (Onni, published in the Vancouver Sun, November 2, 2013) describes The Lookout at Victoria Hill as 115 homes in two four-storey wood-frame buildings at the project location 22 East Royal (Avenue), New Westminster, with a sales centre at 295 Francis Way — the Francis Way address is the sales centre, not the building. Completion year as a finished building: UNCONFIRMED from the sources checked (the profile is a 2013 presale source; treat early information accordingly). Unit count as built, and published restrictions: UNCONFIRMED beyond the profile's 115 homes.
The Carlyle — 280 Ross Drive

Listing sources record the subdivision name The Carlyle (also "Carlyle") at this address, built 2010, in Fraserview NW; current listings describe The Carlyle at Victoria Hill as an award-winning master-planned community building by Onni, concrete construction, with 2 guest suites, gym, clubhouse, bike room, visitor parking and outdoor gardens, and record pets as cats OK at unit level. Unit count and a published building-level restriction set: UNCONFIRMED.
The Grove at Victoria Hill — 265 Ross Drive (listings also at 250, 270 and 275 Ross Drive / Francis Way)

The Grove is documented as one Victoria Hill complex entry across those addresses; the year spread (2008–2011) reflects phased buildings and is flagged, not resolved. Amenities per listings include access to the Boiler House amenity centre (gym, party room, basketball court). Unit count and published restriction set: UNCONFIRMED.
The Whittaker — 225 Francis Way

A current listing names the building The Whittaker in Victoria Hill, records it built 2010, apartment/condo form, freehold strata title, in Fraserview NW, and notes residents' access to the Boiler House amenities (gym, basketball court, theatre, library, party room) in a second listing for the building. Unit count, construction and published restrictions: UNCONFIRMED.
Parkside at Victoria Hill — 271 Francis Way

Current listings name the building Parkside at Victoria Hill by Onni Group, built 2016, concrete construction at unit level, with over 5,400 sq ft of private indoor and outdoor amenity space including a fitness studio, guest suites, party room, games room, bike rooms, outdoor pool and hot tub, in a master-planned community with over 40 acres of dedicated green space. Unit count and published pet/rental/age restrictions: UNCONFIRMED from the sources checked (a strata-registry figure for this building exists only on a banned source and is not used).

items.t: Fraserview NW is the City of New Westminster's Fraserview sub-area: the south slope of mainland New Westminster above the North Arm of the Fraser River, along the Waterfront Esplanade (North Arm) identified in the Official Community Plan parks text. Precise boundary roads are UNVERIFIED, and Fraserview is not listed as a separate City Historic Neighbourhood Context Statement — its City planning treatment is under the OCP mainland schedules, and official City neighbourhood status is UNVERIFIED.

Where the condo stock concentrates: two pockets. (1) The Jamieson Court / Miner Street waterfront-edge pocket on the slope above the North Arm esplanade — Palace Quay (69 / 71 Jamieson Court), Queen's Park Place (55 Blackberry Drive) and Fraserview Park (74 Miner Street). (2) The Victoria Hill master-planned community on the Royal Avenue / Francis Way / Ross Drive hill above Queen's Park — six Onni buildings (Victoria Hill, The Lookout, The Carlyle, The Grove at Victoria Hill, The Whittaker, Parkside at Victoria Hill), all filed by listing sources under Fraserview NW.
SnapStats publishes medians at community level only: New Westminster condos & townhomes median was $560,000 in September 2026 ($587/sqft, 95% sale-to-list, 27 days on market).

Roads and transit: Marine Way / Stewardson Way runs along the south side toward Burnaby and the Queensborough Bridge (Highway 91A); 10th Avenue and 8th Street link the slope to Uptown and Downtown. No SkyTrain station is inside Fraserview; the nearest stations are New Westminster Station and 22nd Street Station (Expo Line), and TransLink route 103 (Quayside / New Westminster Station) serves the Quayside–Fraserview waterfront.

Waterfront anchors: the Waterfront Esplanade (North Arm) and Quayside Park are the waterfront parks serving the slope; the təməsew̓txʷ Aquatic and Community Centre at 65 East Sixth Avenue, the city's main aquatic centre, is up the hill in Uptown, and New Westminster Public Library's Main Branch is at 716 6th Avenue.

blocks.text: Good to know about Fraserview NW

items.t: The sub-area's stock is one developer's hill plus one developer's court. Six of the nine verified apartment entries are Onni's Victoria Hill buildings (2005/2007–2016, sharing the Boiler House amenity centre), and the largest waterfront-edge building, Palace Quay (220 units), is a Bosa building — cross-building comparisons inside this sub-area are unusually direct because so much stock shares two builders.
The Lookout's commonly quoted address is its sales centre.

The townhouse zoning names are routinely gotten wrong for this city. New Westminster's townhouse districts are RT-2 through RT-2C (mainland) and RT-3/3A/3B (Queensborough) under Zoning Bylaw No. 6680, 2001 — an earlier program draft's "RT-A/RT-B" districts do not exist, and the 836.10 m² figure sometimes quoted as a townhouse minimum is an RM-district density threshold (s.462.14). Any Fraserview document using RT-A/RT-B should be sent back.

One Royal Avenue complex wears three addresses and two years. The Victoria Hill building is filed at 15 Royal Avenue (directory, built 2007), at 11 E Royal Avenue under "The Residences Of Victoria Hill," and at 14 E Royal Avenue with a 2005 year in one listing — a buyer searching one address sees a third of the complex's listings.

The Grove is a phase, not a building. Listings place "The Grove" at 250, 265, 270 and 275 Ross Drive / Francis Way with years from 2008 to 2011 — phased low-rise buildings under one community name, so two Grove units can sit in different stratas with different depreciation reports. Compare the specific address's Form B, not the Grove name.
There is almost no detached fallback here.

The city's newest recreation asset is up the hill from both pockets. The təməsew̓txʷ Aquatic and Community Centre at 65 East Sixth Avenue is the city's main aquatic centre, in Uptown — Palace Quay and Victoria Hill listings both cite it, and it is a drive or bus ride (route 103), not a waterfront walk, from Jamieson Court.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Fraserview NW

items.t: : the townhouse districts in New Westminster's Zoning Bylaw No. 6680, 2001 are RT-2, RT-2A, RT-2B and RT-2C (ss.410–413), with RT-3, RT-3A and RT-3B in Queensborough (ss.417–419). Districts named "RT-A" or "RT-B" do NOT exist in this bylaw — any page copy using them is wrong. The RT districts regulate density, height and coverage rather than setting a minimum site area (RT-2, s.410: base density of 18 units per net acre or a floor space ratio of 0.6, height capped at 25 feet, site coverage capped at 40 percent), and the 836.10 m² (9,000 sq. ft.) figure in the bylaw is a density threshold in the RM multiple-dwelling districts (e.g., s.462.14) — an apartment-district figure, NOT a townhouse minimum. Zoning Bylaw No. 6680, 2001 was adopted September 17, 2001 and is consolidated as of June 8, 2026.

Form B diligence (both strata complexes above): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. Listing-level rental/pet lines in are listing data, not bylaws — the Form B and registered bylaws govern.

blocks.text: Good to know about Fraserview NW

items.t: The townhouse zoning names most likely to be quoted at a buyer are wrong. New Westminster has no RT-A or RT-B districts; the bylaw's townhouse districts are RT-2 through RT-2C on the mainland and RT-3/3A/3B in Queensborough, and the 836.10 m² figure sometimes quoted as a townhouse minimum is an apartment-district (RM) density threshold. A listing or page that cites RT-A/RT-B is working from an invented district.

North Arm is a New Westminster board sub-area, not a Richmond one — the esplanade below this slope is New Westminster ground, and comp sets pulled from Richmond's North Arm naming will misprice a Fraserview NW home.

The city's recreation anchor is up the hill, not on the waterfront: the təməsew̓txʷ Aquatic and Community Centre at 65 East Sixth Avenue in Uptown is the city's main aquatic centre, and the Main Branch of New Westminster Public Library is at 716 6th Avenue — waterfront living here still means a hill climb for civic services.
New Westminster runs its own electrical utility — a Fraserview NW home's electricity bill comes from the City, not BC Hydro; a 2026 utility dollar figure confirmed on a City source: UNVERIFIED.

The hospital is across the city: Royal Columbian Hospital, 330 East Columbia Street in Sapperton (Fraser Health), is the city's hospital; a New Westminster Urgent and Primary Care Centre location: UNVERIFIED.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Fraserview NW
Fee-simple lots

items.t: Slope-street house lots (RS districts, Zoning Bylaw No. 6680, 2001, s.310): houses sit in the Single Detached Residential Districts (RS series) — RS-1 sets a minimum site area of 557.40 m² (6,000 sq. ft.) and a floor space ratio of 0.5; the RS districts allow secondary suites, and laneway / carriage houses are regulated under the same bylaw. The RS-1 minimum is a subdivision floor for RS-1 lots, not a claim about any existing lot's size; the zone and dimensions of a specific lot are confirmed parcel by parcel: UNVERIFIED for any individual lot.

Townhouse-district ground (RT family — stated correctly): the bylaw's townhouse districts are RT-2, RT-2A, RT-2B and RT-2C (ss.410–413), with RT-3, RT-3A and RT-3B in Queensborough (ss.417–419); the RT districts regulate density, height and coverage rather than setting a minimum site area or frontage (RT-2, s.410: base density of 18 units per net acre or a floor space ratio of 0.6, height capped at 25 feet and site coverage at 40 percent). RT-A and RT-B do not exist in this bylaw. Apartment buildings sit on the Quayside / Jamieson Court waterfront edge under the RM multiple-dwelling districts.

Serviced position: New Westminster operates its own electrical utility and City water / sewer services — the sub-area's established lots sit inside the City's serviced system on that wording; servicing for any single vacant or assembly parcel is confirmed with the City, UNCONFIRMED parcel-by-parcel here. A 2026 utility dollar figure for a Fraserview home confirmed on a City source: UNVERIFIED.

ALR vs non-ALR: no Agricultural Land Reserve land is identified in Fraserview in the sources read; ALR status for a specific property is checked in the Agricultural Land Commission's ALR Property and Map Finder. No ALR percentage split is stated.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Fraserview NW

items.t: OCP — Our City 2041, Bylaw No. 7925 (2017): the City's Official Community Plan governs the area, including its Development Permit Areas (Schedule B) for the mainland. Fraserview has no separate City neighbourhood plan in the sources read — its planning treatment is under the OCP mainland schedules.

Zoning — Zoning Bylaw No. 6680 (2001): RS series (s.310) for detached lots (RS-1: minimum site area 557.40 m² / 6,000 sq. ft.) figure in the bylaw is a density threshold in the RM multiple-dwelling districts (e.g., s.462.14), not a townhouse minimum — any page or pitch that presents 836.10 m² as an RT figure, or names an RT-A/RT-B district, is wrong on the bylaw itself.

Subdivision + servicing — VERIFIED: New Westminster Subdivision and Development Control Bylaw No. 7142, 2007 regulates the subdivision of lands and establishes the standard of works and services to be provided in respect of subdivisions and developments (effective March 12, 2007; consolidated September 25, 2023). All subdivisions require approval by the City's Approving Officer, and the subdivision process ensures new lots are adequately serviced with water, sewers, underground electrical, communications, street lighting, roads, sidewalks, street trees and other City requirements, meet the Zoning Bylaw's minimum lot size and frontage requirements, and are consistent with the OCP.

Floodplain diligence — stated precisely, as the research documents it: the City states that both Queensborough and sections of the mainland are included within the provincial floodplain, and that the city covers twelve square kilometres of which five are within the flood boundaries on the Ministry of Environment Floodplain Map; the City's floodplain study Zone 2 covers the historically commercial and industrial Fraser River land at the west end of the city. No floodplain zone number is assigned to Fraserview's residential slope in the research, and lot-level flood status for a Fraserview property: UNVERIFIED — check with the City.

Strata diligence (waterfront-edge stock): for strata purchases on the esplanade edge, review depreciation and contingency under the provincial strata framework early; BC strata disputes can go to the Civil Resolution Tribunal. The full BC strata block applies to any strata lot: Form B diligence (fees, amounts owed, levies, CRF balance, insurance summary; provided within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page); depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since November 24, 2022 (short-term restrictions may still apply by bylaw); only 55+ age bylaws valid under SPA ss.123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions; a "45+" listing line is NOT a valid BC age bylaw.

ALR rules (for completeness — no Fraserview ALR land is identified here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR. Check the parcel on ALC mapping before applying any of this.

New Westminster property taxes: City of New Westminster 2026 property taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty on current taxes remaining unpaid on July 3, 2026 and a second 5% penalty on any unpaid balance on September 3, 2026. New Westminster operates its own electrical utility.

blocks.text: Good to know about Fraserview NW

items.t: The city runs its own power: New Westminster operates its own electrical utility alongside City water and sewer services — a servicing and billing difference from every neighbouring municipality that surfaces in closing adjustments and in subdivision servicing discussions under Bylaw No. 7142.

Five of the city's twelve square kilometres are inside the flood boundaries: the City states the mainland sections point plainly — Queensborough and sections of the mainland are within the provincial floodplain — yet no zone number is published for Fraserview's residential slope in the research (Zone 2 in the City study is the west-end commercial/industrial river land). The honest diligence line is a City check on the specific lot, not a zone label borrowed from another sub-area.

The 2021 Census counted 78,916 people in New Westminster, up 11.2% from 70,996 in 2016, at a density of 5,052 people per sq. km — citywide context only; a Fraserview-only population figure: UNVERIFIED.

Page-statement check for this area. Approved page claims, where a live page states them, are the settled set only: REALTOR since 2015; 10 straight years in the FVREB Medallion Club; Top 1% of Fraser Valley Realtors; #1 in South Surrey/White Rock by MLS points for 2025 and 2026 YTD; more than $500M in sales.

faq.q: Is Fraserview NW the same as Vancouver's Fraserview?
faq.a: No. Fraserview NW is New Westminster's Fraserview sub-area, on the south slope above the North Arm of the Fraser River in the City of New Westminster (School District 40); Vancouver's Fraserview is a separate Vancouver East sub-area covered in its own file.

faq.q: What sold in Fraserview NW in September 2026?
faq.a: Detached: 0 solds from 2 listings, so the sales ratio is not applicable (0 solds); condos & townhomes: 10 solds from 53 listings (19%). At the New Westminster community level the detached median sale price was $1,365,000 and the condos & townhomes median was $560,000 (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats GVR September 2026 report).

faq.q: Which schools serve a Fraserview NW address?
faq.a: For the sample address 1010 Hamilton Street, the SD40 locator result is Lord Kelvin Elementary, Fraser River Middle and New Westminster Secondary, with Early French Immersion at École Lord Tweedsmuir Elementary; catchments are address-based.

faq.q: How do Fraserview residents get to SkyTrain?
faq.a: There is no station inside the sub-area; TransLink route 103 (Quayside / New Westminster Station) serves the waterfront, and the nearest Expo Line stations are New Westminster Station and 22nd Street Station.

faq.q: What condo stock does the sub-area actually have?
faq.a: Nine verified apartment-condo entries in two pockets: Palace Quay, Queen's Park Place and Fraserview Park on the Jamieson Court / Miner Street waterfront edge, and six Victoria Hill buildings on the hill (Victoria Hill, The Lookout, The Carlyle, The Grove at Victoria Hill, The Whittaker, Parkside at Victoria Hill) — plus Victoria Hill's Francis Way townhomes.

faq.q: Is Palace Quay one building or two?
faq.a: One complex at two addresses — 69 and 71 Jamieson Court — with 220 units per both the building directory and the furnished-rental directory. Sources disagree on the year (1991 in the rental directory and several listings, 1992 in the directory, 1993 in one listing); the builder is recorded as Bosa Development and the form as an 18-storey concrete high-rise. Verify the strata plan number for the specific unit before relying on a year.

faq.q: Can I live at Queen's Park Place if I am under 55?
faq.a: The building is published as a 55+ building (55 Blackberry Drive, built 1994). A 55+ bylaw under SPA ss.123.1/123.2 is the one valid age bylaw in BC, and its exemptions cover legacy residents, live-in caregivers and (from May 1, 2023) younger spouses/partners and defined children of a 55+ resident. Whether you qualify is a Form B / filed-bylaw question — read them before writing.

faq.q: Can I rent out a Palace Quay or Victoria Hill unit long-term?
faq.a: Yes — strata rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable since November 24, 2022 anywhere in BC, even though both buildings' directory lines read "rentals allowed w/restrictions." Short-term rentals are different: a bylaw can still restrict them, and the registered bylaws on the Form B govern that question.

faq.q: Fraser Mews is listed as a townhouse — is it one?
faq.a: No. Some listings carry Sub-Type Townhouse, others Apartment; the built form is a 4-storey elevator building with underground parking, so it is an apartment strata with townhouse-style ground units. Diligence is apartment diligence (elevator, parkade, building envelope), whatever the sub-type field says.

faq.q: Can I rent out my Fraserview NW townhouse?
faq.a: Long-term, yes under provincial law: strata rental-restriction bylaws have been void since Nov 24, 2022, even where a directory still prints a restriction line. Short-term rentals can still be restricted by bylaw — read the registered bylaws in the Form B package.

faq.q: Which schools serve a Jamieson Court or Victoria Hill address?
faq.a: Address-based in SD40. The verified locator run for the sample address 1010 Hamilton Street returned Lord Kelvin Elementary, Fraser River Middle and New Westminster Secondary — run the exact address; waterfront-edge addresses can differ.

faq.q: Is flood risk a real diligence item on the waterfront edge?
faq.a: Yes. The City states sections of the mainland sit inside the provincial floodplain and five of the city's twelve square kilometres fall within the Ministry flood boundaries — confirm the specific building's flood construction level and insurance position with the City before subjects come off.
